faqs.a: An .ico is a container: a 6-byte header, then a 16-byte directory entry per image describing its size and position, then the image data itself. Each entry can be a PNG or a classic Windows BMP (DIB) bitmap.

Modern icons embed PNG images (the Vista+ format). Older icons store BMP/DIB bitmaps with a separate transparency mask. This editor decodes both: PNG entries display directly, and 24/32-bit BMP entries are decoded pixel by pixel.
faqs.q: What is the difference between PNG and BMP entries?

faqs.a: Yes — tick exactly the layers you want and press Rebuild. The selected layers are re-encoded as PNGs and packed into a fresh .ico with the same hand-written encoder the converter uses.
faqs.q: Can I remove sizes from an .ico?

faqs.a: Press the PNG button on any layer card to download that single size as a standalone PNG image.
faqs.q: How do I extract one size as a PNG?

faqs.a: Only 24-bit and 32-bit BMP entries are decoded. Rarer formats (1/4/8-bit paletted, JPEG-compressed entries) are listed honestly as unsupported and skipped.

The transparency (AND) mask is not applied — BMP layers show their raw color data. PNG layers keep full alpha. If a BMP layer looks like it has a black background, that is the missing mask, not a bug.

ico-editor.formula:
ICO = 6-byte header + 16 bytes per entry + image data
Entry bytes: width(1) height(1) colors(1) reserved(1) planes(2) bpp(2) size(4) offset(4)
BMP inside ICO: BITMAPINFOHEADER, biHeight = 2 x image height (color + mask)
Example: 2 layers (16, 32) -> header bytes 0-5, entries bytes 6-37, image data from byte 38.
howTo: Choose a Windows .ico file from your device (up to 10 MB).
The editor lists every embedded layer: size, format (PNG/BMP), bit depth, and byte size.
Download any single layer as a PNG with the button on its card.
Tick the layers you want to keep and press Rebuild for a leaner .ico.
Press Download rebuilt to save the new icon file.

ico-editor.workedExample:
You open a 2-layer icon (16 and 32 px).
Header bytes 0–5, two 16-byte entries at bytes 6–37, image data from byte 38.
Layer 1 is a 32-bit BMP entry: its BITMAPINFOHEADER reports biHeight = 64 (2 x 32 for color + mask).
You download the 32 px layer as PNG and rebuild a 1-layer .ico.
